summary: The empty-set idempotent in Theorem5.3 fails in an explicit C2 example; the existential theorem is not refuted and the nonempty-set construction/main applications survive.
version_scope: UEA 94983 Accepted Version, filename 18April2024, PDF creation metadata 2023-10-11 separately recorded

problems.title: Empty-set idempotent does not realize the stipulated stabilizer
problems.source_location: PDF/printed p16 Theorem5.3 every finite X; p17 specified e_X and H_e claim; pp18-20 marked-component argument and final automorphism identification
problems.assumptions: G=H=C2=<a|a^2=1>, A={a}, B={a}, X=empty; satisfies finite presentation, finite generation and monoid-generating assumptions.
problems.check: Empty product e=1, Stab_G(empty)=C2. a is a unit and a^-1=a. u=yay^-1 satisfies u²=1 from a defining relator. The unit au maps to the cyclically reduced word ay ay^-1 in C2*F(y,z); its nth power has free-product syllable length4n, so au has infinite order. H_1=U(M) is infinite.
problems.result: H_e is not isomorphic to the finite stabilizer for this specified e. This is a counterexample to the construction claim at empty X.
problems.counterevidence: For nonempty X the doubly marked vertex set anchors the distinguished G component. In this same example X={1} yields another H-class isomorphic to C2, so the existential theorem itself is not refuted.
problems.impact: Localized proof/construction boundary. Theorem5.4, Cor5.8 and Cor5.12 only need nonempty finite sets.
problems.correction: Restrict verified construction/theorem scope to nonempty finite X. Retaining all finite X requires a separate general empty-set realization in the same M; not supplied here.
problems.repair_verification: Analytic normal-form counterexample and nonempty-scope repair; original full quantifier remains unresolved.
